messages:
anya: Heads up — seeing abnormally small batch sizes (~1-3) on v2-quant and v2-fp16 variants after KV warmup window. Looks like compat-set fragmentation + token-budget cap are starving coalescing.
joel: Can you share p50/p95 latency and batch-size histogram? also which queue_policy is active on those pools?
anya: p50=18ms, p95=120ms. batch-size histogram: 60% size 1, 25% size 2, 15% >=3. queue_policy=`fair-share` on that pool. token_budget target is 2048 currently.
ravi: That histogram screams compat-set splintering. If multi-variant routing creates many tiny compat sets, scheduler never sees compatible peers to merge. token_budget only helps if compatible requests exist.
lisa: Also saw kernel+padding penalty when merging quantized and fp16 on the same batch — kernel selection flips to a conservative path which increases per-token latencies. we should avoid mixing kernels unless we can force a faster path.
joel: Can you paste a sample trace? any logs for "compat_match" or "kernel_fallback"?
anya: quick excerpt: `sched: req=abcd compat_set_size=1 chosen_variant=v2-quant kernel=quant_fallback kv_hit=true token_budget=210`
infra-bot: deploy: canary update pushed to pool gpu-eu-2 for config `compat_merge=false` (deploy-id: deploy-227).
ravi: Proposed quick experiments: 1) enable `compat_merge=true` in canary (10%) to allow cross-variant merging when safe; 2) bump token_budget to 4096 for the canary pool; 3) add scheduler tracepoint for compat_set membership and kv_hit ratio per request.
lisa: +1. I'll also add kernel-selection tagging in traces (`kernel_hint=fast_kernel` vs `kernel_fallback`) so we can filter latency regressions to kernel switches.
joel: Note risk: if compat_merge forces kernel conversions, we could regress throughput. We should add a per-variant kernel-compat whitelist so only variants with matching kernel ABI are merged.
anya: Good call. For canary: compat_merge=true but with `kernel_abi_whitelist: ["quant", "quant_v2"]`. Ravi can we add throttle logic: only allow compat_merge when compat_set_size>=2 AND avg_seq_len within 20%?
ravi: Yep. I'll prototype using existing queue matcher (PR 8423). Pseudoconfig: ```
queue_policy: prefer-oldest
compat_merge: true
compat_min_size: 2
compat_seq_len_ratio: 0.2
token_budget_per_batch: 4096
kernel_abi_whitelist: ["quant","quant_v2"]
```
lisa: I'll instrument metrics: `batch_size_by_variant`, `compat_merge_attempts`, `kernel_switch_rate`, `kv_hit_ratio`. Planning dashboards and a regression alert on p95 > 1.2x baseline.
joel: Also add a small synthetic workload that sends mixed-variant requests with prefix sharing to validate KV warmup behavior — we saw warmup increased compat_set fragmentation earlier.
anya: Action items: @lisa own telemetry, add tracepoints + dashboard; @ravi run canary and open PR 8423; @joel review kernel whitelist logic; I'll monitor p50/p95 and batch histogram.
anya: One more note: if compat_merge doesn't help, next step is adaptive token-budget per compat-set: lower budget for tiny sets to avoid skew, and raise for larger later. But try simpler knobs first.
lisa: I'll post the dashboard link when traces are in. Expect initial canary results in ~2 hours. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
ravi: Starting canary rollout now (10%). I'll post logs.
infra-bot: metric_alert: canary-p95 > baseline (1.05x) — but batch_size mean increased from 1.2 -> 2.9 for canary.
anya: Interesting — batch size went up and p95 barely moved. sounds promising. Keep monitoring for kernel-induced tail.
joel: If tail appears, we can gate compat_merge by `kernel_switch_rate < 0.05` for a few minutes.
lisa: Noted. I'll add that gate to the canary config.
anya: Thanks team. We'll reconvene if infra-bot posts any more alerts.
